review_notes:
I read all of OmegaPerm.lean (lines 1–116). Only `omegaSkeinRep_eq` has real proof content. Its induction over `MonoidAlgebra.induction_on` has a generator case and short additivity and scalar cases. The additive and scalar cases are two-line parallel uses of `Functor.map_add` and `Functor.map_smul`. That is routine, and inside the file it is not nontrivial reasoning repeated in two proofs. The other declarations (`omegaPermHom`, `omegaSkeinRep`, `omegaSkeinRep_of`) are one-line definitions or direct API applications, so they give no duplication either.

I also grepped the repo for the same induction pattern. Near-copies of the add/smul-passing induction exist in Deligne/IndSchurKilled.lean (around lines 242–253) and Deligne/SchurTransport.lean (around lines 426–437). Both are outside the target file. Neither is a second copy of the target's reasoning, because they work with `indOf` and `indOfPowIso`, not `P.ω` and `skeinRep`. I did not inspect SkeinTower.lean (257) or BlockTower.lean (250) beyond the grep preview; they use the same induction but also look specific to their own setting. A shared lemma would need a precise statement and rewrites of both uses under their own hypotheses, and I could not justify that from the sources. The remaining uncertainty is whether `omegaSkeinRep_eq` could be shortened by showing `ω.map ∘ skeinRep` is an algebra homomorphism. That would be a possible simplification, but it is not repeated machinery.
